sourceSpanDistribution.note: Incremental-mode raw reports show both tools independently landing on the SAME real source lines in GCD.swift: MutantKit line 29 (x2, distinct relational-operator variants of the same '<' site), 31, 35, 49 (x2); Muter line 29, 31, 35, 49 (x2). This is a real, high-confidence line-level overlap neither tool's own report can be used to auto-confirm today (see comparability note above).

comparability.note: Both tools independently found the SAME real source lines (29, 31, 35, 49, 49 in the incremental-mode GCD.swift) with the same operator family (RelationalOperatorReplacement) -- a real, high-confidence overlap by line+operator that the current matching key cannot confirm, because Muter's real report.json never includes mutationSnapshot (before/after text), only mutationPoint+testSuiteOutcome (confirmed against Muter's own CodingKeys). Cross-tool matching relies on text hashes, not line/column, by design -- so this is an honest, expected 'not confirmable' result given real data, never a fabricated match.

causalFinding.question: What dominates MutantKit's 580.8s?
causalFinding.answer: B: isolated fallback is 100% of the workload in this run -- ALL 14 mutant executions across all 3 modes ran under executionMode=isolated (0 schemata), confirmed directly from MutantKit's own real report.json per-mutant field. RelationalOperatorReplacement is not schemata-eligible today (only bool-literal-inversion is). Baseline cost is a small, consistent fraction (~15-20% of each mode's total: 29-41s of 168-210s); per-mutant build+test sums (~78-80% of total) dominate. Confirmation/differential-validation and report-parsing overhead are comparatively small (external wall vs MutantKit's own internal startedAt/finishedAt differ by only ~2-5s per mode).
causalFinding.evidence: Computed directly from each mode's raw report.json: results[].executionMode, results[].buildDurationSeconds, results[].testDurationSeconds, baseline.buildDurationSeconds/testDurationSeconds, startedAt/finishedAt -- never inferred or estimated.
causalFinding.implication: Cache-based improvements (schemata build/result cache) would not help here, since isolated mode's own rebuild-per-mutant cost -- not a cache-miss cost -- is what's being paid. Schemata-izing RelationalOperatorReplacement (or another common operator) is the change with real, evidenced leverage on this specific bottleneck.

explicitCaveats: pipeline calibration only, not a performance conclusion

MutantKit and Muter operator sets are not identical (Muter has no bool-literal-inversion; this run scoped both to their one shared operator, RelationalOperatorReplacement, so operator sets ARE matched for this specific run, but mutation counts still differ slightly: 4-6 for MutantKit vs 3-5 for Muter, a real per-tool discovery difference on the same source, not yet root-caused)
diskBytesWritten was unavailable in this run (unwired at the time) -- fixed in a follow-up commit, not retroactively backfilled into this baseline
not a cross-tool performance conclusion -- MutantKit and Muter costs are reported side by side for calibration purposes only

bugsFoundAndFixed.description: ResultNormalizer.normalizeMuterReport required an applied['mutationSnapshot']['before'/'after'] field. Confirmed against Muter's own source (Sources/muterCore/TestReporting/MuterTestReport.swift AppliedMutationOperator.CodingKeys) that this field is explicitly excluded from JSON encoding, at any version -- it never exists in a real report. Every real Muter mutation was silently dropped as a result (0 discovered/killed/survived reported despite 3 real mutations existing in the raw report).

bugsFoundAndFixed.description: The workflow's --mutantkit-source-include "Sources/IntegerUtilities/**" matched the whole 6-file module (83 real ROR mutations, confirmed via a local `mutantkit plan`), not just GCD.swift. At isolated-mode cost that is a real 1.5-3 hour run, which blew past the 900-second per-invocation timeout and produced no report at all for MutantKit.

bugsFoundAndFixed.description: ResultNormalizer read integrity?["passed"] as a JSON key. IntegrityReport.passed (Sources/MutationModel/Integrity.swift) is a computed property (violations.isEmpty), never a stored/serialized field -- the key can never exist in real report.json. Every real MutantKit run was silently marked correctness-FAILED regardless of actual data (0 violations, all counts consistent).
bugsFoundAndFixed.fix: Derived integrityPassed as violations.isEmpty, matching MutantKit's own real semantics
